findings.claim: Nested-spawn request prepares a child lease and returns prepared; dispatch is a separate execute-worker action.
findings.impact: A prepared receipt is not evidence a worker started.

findings.claim: Current main increments spawn-tree consumed token/wall counters by grants before execution and does not pass the spawn grant to nested lease as an enforced runtime budget.
findings.status: BEVESTIGD; BRANCH FIXED WITH LIMITED ENFORCEMENT
findings.branch_change: Grants are reservations; measured usage is recorded per nested completion only when reported. Missing usage remains unknown. The nested token grant constrains post-run evaluation/admission but is not a hard mid-inference provider cap.

findings.claim: Canonical worker settlement exists, but current-main sub_agent_spawns terminal projection is only explicitly updated in ProofRunService; recovery holds exist for uncertain external execution.
findings.status: PARTIALLY BEVESTIGD; BRANCH ADDS NORMAL PROJECTION
findings.branch_change: LoopService settles nested spawn projection after canonical worker lease status updates and skips ordinary non-nested leases.

findings.claim: ToolBroker policy evaluation is not observed as mediation of CLI-internal tool calls; runtime adapters invoke external CLI processes with runtime-specific controls.
findings.status: BEVESTIGD AS MEDIATION GAP; ISOLATION VARIES
findings.impact: ToolBroker unit tests do not establish interception of tools initiated inside external runtime processes.

findings.claim: Skills can be injected into compatible maker assignments and credited only after delivery/invocation/digest/check/verification evidence; memory access logging proves selection/assembly, not causal use or uplift.

Fitness view filters/weights signals and caps Gym contribution, while the older Gym evaluation still averages differently scaled metrics with inconsistent direction; no evidence shows Gym score drives separate Evolve selection.
findings.impact: Do not use the Gym aggregate as a comparable task-quality or promotion measure.

findings.claim: PR #1231 adds poller runtime-failure reporting but remains open and is absent from current main; current-main poller logs locally and server readiness derives lapsed claims.
findings.impact: Historical green checks do not prove present production poller or browser state.

findings.claim: Explainer bundle can bind source commit, but per-fact graph evidence drops scan/commit/source/synthetic/freshness/method lineage and uses generic graph references.
findings.impact: Synthetic test fixtures do not establish that production graph input is synthetic.

findings.claim: DjimitSec source contains fixed-scope scan, separate verifier, validated finding import and reconciliation; live finding→repair→deployed release→retest closure not observed.
findings.impact: Collected scanner observations and imported work items do not prove verified remediation.

findings.claim: Funnel and skill route distinguish lifecycle stages and UI warns activity is not durable improvement; system-wide net value and transfer remain unproven.
findings.impact: Proposal/review/applied counts are not a universal net-value metric; reported causal labels are not promotion evidence.

findings.claim: Nested child budget reservation and spawn identity were not durable before worktree/lease preparation, so a crash could leave untraceable reservations or duplicate a preparation on retry.
findings.branch_change: Reservation and requested intent now commit together with planned lease ID; idempotency keys bind a canonical request fingerprint; preparation is reconciled only when the planned canonical lease exists. If absence of side effects cannot be proven, intent and budget remain held; automatic retry/cleanup is not implemented.
findings.impact: Prevents duplicate dispatch and budget release on ambiguous preparation, while an interrupted no-lease intent can consume capacity pending operator recovery.

findings.claim: A depth-enabled tree with a total budget at or below the root grant could reserve the entire budget for the root and make child work impossible.
findings.branch_change: When nesting is enabled the root receives at most half of viable token/wall budgets; configurations below 2 tokens or 2000ms reject before preparation.

findings.claim: Nested token grants are not enforceable as hard in-flight inference caps across the supported external CLI adapters.
findings.impact: Reported maker usage is compared to the grant in the post-run token gate; missing usage skips that gate. The current inference call is not stopped at the grant, and not every nested role uses this maker gate.
findings.decision: Do not claim a hard token cap. Adapter-specific enforcement requires separately verified CLI/provider contracts.
